value.rationale: The exact natural design invariant is the smallest mean-square two-step amplification attainable without changing the uniform stage marginals. It exhibits two structurally determined phase boundaries and an almost tenfold contraction gain at r=2 versus antithetic pairing. The distinction between antithetic stages and antithetic squared-response ranks is relevant to stability-aware coupling choices; the result does not assert universal nonlinear usefulness.
